world.headline: Iran says its 'maximum deterrence' plan is ready; calls the US reply on Hormuz 'unconvincing'
world.summary: Al Jazeera reports that Iran says the US response to its Strait of Hormuz proposal is unconvincing and that a 'maximum deterrence' plan is ready in case of any new US attack. A headline on the same site says Trump confirmed strikes, but I could not read the details. China says it backs US-Iran negotiation efforts.

sources.name: Al Jazeera (front page and live blog, Nov 4)

world.headline: Israel: opposition leaders back Eisenkot to unseat Netanyahu
world.summary: Israeli opposition leaders have thrown their support behind Gadi Eisenkot as the candidate to oust Prime Minister Benjamin Netanyahu, Al Jazeera reports. Separately, Israeli forces detained dozens of Palestinians across the occupied West Bank on Nov 4.

world.headline: Sudan: displaced families fear famine as aid situation worsens
world.summary: Al Jazeera reports a mounting food crisis in Sudan, with warnings of famine and displaced people saying the aid situation is getting worse. I could not retrieve casualty or hunger figures.

world.headline: Ukraine: Russian strike on a Zaporizhzhia school killed 24 (reported Nov 3)
world.summary: Ukrainian emergency services said Russian bombing hit a school in a Zaporizhzhia-region village on Monday, killing 24. Both Ukraine and Russia also said their emergency alert apps were hacked and sent false raid and chemical or nuclear warnings. I found no newer reporting on this today.

world.headline: Indonesia's Supreme Court invalidates the vice president's school certificate (reported Nov 3)
world.summary: The court overturned two lower-court rulings and invalidated the equivalency certificate Vice President Gibran Rakabuming Raka used for his 2024 candidacy. It raises questions about his future in office, though removal would need separate constitutional proceedings.

japan.headline: DPFP says it cannot back the food consumption-tax cut bill as written
japan.summary: Democratic Party for the People leader Yuichiro Tamaki said on Nov 4 that supporting the government's bill to cut the consumption tax on food, paired with an income-linked benefit program, is impossible in its current form. The party will decide after seeing whether the government and ruling coalition accept its alternative, which calls for resident and income tax cuts; talks have made little progress. The tax cut would end in April 2029.

japan.headline: Opposition presses Takaichi over skipping an online G7 summit
japan.summary: Opposition parties are stepping up criticism of Prime Minister Sanae Takaichi for missing an online G7 summit in early October, calling her and the Foreign Ministry's explanations vague. Some suspect a dinner with LDP executives just beforehand. The article links this to the October resignation of agriculture minister Kazuo Yana.

japan.headline: North Korea fires multiple missiles toward the Sea of Japan
japan.summary: South Korea's military said North Korea fired multiple missiles from the Sondok area of South Hamgyong province toward the Sea of Japan on Wednesday, Nov 4. The type, ballistic or cruise, was not specified in the report I read.

japan.headline: Disaster minister visits Kumamoto as the new disaster agency settles in
japan.summary: Disaster Management Minister Hosono visited Kumamoto on Nov 4, according to a headline on Nippon.com. The new national disaster management agency began operating on Nov 2. I only saw the headline, not the article.

japan.headline: Business: Mitsui Chemicals eyes a bid for JSR worth over ¥1 trillion
japan.summary: Nippon.com lists a Nov 4 report that Mitsui Chemicals is considering acquiring JSR for more than ¥1 trillion. It also lists a report that Japanese police detected Chinese malware in Android TV devices. I only saw headlines for both.

us.headline: Democrats win Congress in the midterms, per CBS projections
us.summary: CBS projected Democrats take the House (it estimates 251 to 268 seats) and the Senate (at least 54 seats), with Alaska and Mississippi still uncalled and about 75 House races open as of Wednesday morning. Reported Senate flips include Texas (Talarico over Paxton), Kansas, Maine, Ohio, Iowa and South Carolina. These are live-blog figures and will change. The Supreme Court had on Nov 2 rejected the Trump administration's request to set aside about 20,000 California ballots.

us.headline: Vance blames the Iran war for Republican losses; Trump says he'd have won if on the ballot
us.summary: Vice President Vance wrote that voters left the ticket over the Iran war and the cost of living. Trump said 'if I was on the ballot, we would have won,' said he would accept the results, and said Defense Secretary Hegseth is doing a good job and is not being removed, though CBS reported he asked advisers about it. Speaker Mike Johnson will not run for minority leader and Steve Scalise will.

us.headline: What Democrats say they will do first: Medicaid, ACA credits, tariffs, the Iran war
us.summary: Democrats say they will move to reverse the Medicaid cuts, restore expired ACA premium subsidies, end tariffs and press Trump to end the Iran war or seek authorization. House Democrats also gain subpoena and investigative power; Hakeem Jeffries promised action starting in January.

us.headline: Space: NASA's Swift telescope falls to Earth; Artemis II launch disturbed the upper atmosphere
us.summary: Space.com reports NASA's Swift space telescope crashed back to Earth on Nov 4, three months after a planned private boost to a higher orbit failed. A separate report says the Artemis II moon launch tore a large hole in the upper atmosphere that disrupted GPS signals.

us.headline: AI and politics: PAC spending in Congress, and OpenAI eyeing 2028
us.summary: TechCrunch published pieces on how AI-industry PACs spent millions trying to shape Congress and how they fared, and on OpenAI already trying to shape the 2028 election. Other tech headlines: Meta is acquiring AI coding startup Conductor, and CrowdStrike is paying nearly $500M for two AI security startups. I only saw headlines, not the articles.
